title: [Day 04] Incremental DOM mutations
text:
Part 2 is in. Each observer callback is now resolved as removes, then adds, then attributes, then text.

Why that order: the callback runs after the whole turn, so the raw records are intermediate steps. Removes go first, using the parent from before the callback, so the player detaches a node before inserting anything at `nextId`. Adds go second, and only the top connected node of a new subtree is serialized, which is why a nested add appears once and a move keeps its old id. Attributes and text go last and keep only the final value on nodes that remain and were not just serialized.

Same-batch cases covered: add-then-remove produces nothing, a move keeps its id, a nested add is serialized once, a repeated attribute keeps the last value. Masking, blocking, `on*` attributes, and script content follow the Day 03 rules. See ADR 0023.

Checks that passed: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`.

Left open: Parts 3–5 (position tests, the rebuild helper, and the seeded fuzz test).
